answer: Random Marble Assignment**. Each round, a verifiable random beacon assigns agents to tasks; assignments are secret until a commit cutoff, so identities cannot coordinate which agent gets which slot. An attacker cannot forge predictable task placement before the beacon fires. Because only one assignment per identity counts and duplicates in the same slot are voided, mass-registering agents fails to raise the tide of successful completions. Each extra identity costs a registration deposit plus recurring beacon-wait overhead, making sybils strictly negative-yield.
